disclaimer: Official CBSE information is maintained strictly separate from analytical priority guidance. No chapter should be skipped based on analytical tags.

assessmentStructure.practical: 30 Marks (Two experiments 7+7, Practical record 5, One activity from any section 3, Investigatory project 3, Viva on experiments/activities/project 5)
assessmentStructure.questionPaperDesign: ~50% Competency-based (MCQ, Case-based, Source-based integrated questions), ~20% Select response (MCQs), ~30% Constructed response (Short/Long answer)

coreTopics: Electric charges and their conservation
Coulomb's law force between two point charges, forces between multiple charges, superposition principle
Continuous charge distribution
Electric field, electric field due to a point charge, electric field lines
Electric dipole, electric field due to a dipole on axial and equatorial lines
Torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field
Electric flux and statement of Gauss's theorem
Gauss theorem applications: field due to infinitely long straight wire, uniformly charged infinite plane sheet
keyDerivations: Electric field on axial and equatorial lines of electric dipole
Torque on dipole in uniform electric field (tau = p x E)
Electric field due to infinitely long charged wire using Gauss's Law
Electric field due to infinite charged plane sheet using Gauss's Law
chapters.numericalFocus: Superposition of electrostatic forces, dipole torque, flux through closed surfaces and Gauss law calculations
diagrams: Electric field lines patterns
Electric dipole configurations
Gaussian cylinder and pillbox surfaces
chapters.practicalLinkage: Verification of electrostatic properties using electroscope and electric field mapping

coreTopics: Electric potential, potential difference, electric potential due to a point charge, electric dipole and system of charges
Equipotential surfaces, electrical potential energy of a system of two point charges and of electric dipoles in an electrostatic field
Conductors and dielectrics, free charges and bound charges inside a conductor
Dielectrics and electric polarization, capacitors and capacitance
Combination of capacitors in series and in parallel
Capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with and without dielectric medium between the plates
Energy stored in a capacitor
keyDerivations: Potential due to a point charge and electric dipole
Potential energy of dipole in uniform external field
Parallel plate capacitor capacitance formula (C = epsilon_0 * A / d)
Capacitance with dielectric slab between plates
Energy stored in charged capacitor (U = 1/2 C V^2) and energy density
chapters.numericalFocus: Equivalent capacitance in series-parallel circuits, dielectric insertion effects on charge and voltage, energy calculations
diagrams: Equipotential surfaces for point charges and dipoles
Parallel plate capacitor with dielectric slab
chapters.practicalLinkage: Determination of capacitance using bridge circuits, multimeter measurements

coreTopics: Electric current, flow of electric charges in a metallic conductor, drift velocity, mobility and their relation with electric current
Ohm's law, V-I characteristics (linear and non-linear), electrical energy and power, electrical resistivity and conductivity
Temperature dependence of resistance
Internal resistance of a cell, potential difference and emf of a cell, combination of cells in series and in parallel
Kirchhoff's rules and simple applications
Wheatstone bridge (principle and balanced condition)
keyDerivations: Relation between current and drift velocity (I = n e A v_d)
Deduction of Ohm's law and resistivity expression (rho = m / (n e^2 tau))
Terminal voltage vs emf relation (V = E - I r)
Wheatstone bridge balance condition (P/Q = R/S)
chapters.numericalFocus: Kirchhoff loop rules in multi-loop circuits, cell combinations for maximum current, temperature coefficient of resistance
diagrams: Wheatstone bridge circuit schematic
V-I graphs for ohmic and non-ohmic conductors
chapters.practicalLinkage: To determine resistivity of two wires using meter bridge, compare EMF of two cells, find internal resistance

units.unitName: Magnetic Effects of Current, Magnetism, EMI and AC

coreTopics: Concept of magnetic field, Oersted's experiment
Biot-Savart law and its application to current carrying circular loop
Ampere's law and its applications to infinitely long straight wire and straight solenoid
Force on a moving charge in uniform magnetic and electric fields (Lorentz force)
Force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field
Force between two parallel current-carrying conductors - definition of ampere
Torque experienced by a current loop in uniform magnetic field
Moving coil galvanometer - its current sensitivity and conversion to ammeter and voltmeter
keyDerivations: Biot-Savart Law on the axis of a circular current loop
Magnetic field of long solenoid using Ampere's circuital law
Force between two parallel current-carrying conductors
Torque on current loop in magnetic field (tau = M x B)
Conversion of galvanometer to ammeter (shunt resistance) and voltmeter (series resistance)
chapters.numericalFocus: Galvanometer conversion shunts, force between parallel wires, circular path radius of charge in B field
diagrams: Moving coil galvanometer assembly
Right-hand thumb rule and magnetic field vectors
chapters.practicalLinkage: Conversion of galvanometer to ammeter and voltmeter in laboratory

coreTopics: Bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid, magnetic field lines
Magnetic dipole moment of a revolving electron
Magnetization and magnetic intensity
Magnetic properties of materials: Paramagnetic, diamagnetic and ferromagnetic substances with examples
Effect of temperature on magnetic properties (Curie temperature statement)
keyDerivations: Magnetic dipole moment of revolving electron (Bohr magneton)
Axial and equatorial field of a bar magnet
chapters.numericalFocus: Magnetic susceptibility, relative permeability and permeability relation (mu_r = 1 + chi)
diagrams: Magnetic field lines of bar magnet vs solenoid
Alignment of dipoles in dia, para, and ferromagnetic materials
chapters.practicalLinkage: Deflection magnetometer and magnetic compass field lines mapping

coreTopics: Electromagnetic induction: Faraday's experiments and laws, induced EMF and current
Lenz's Law and conservation of energy
Motional EMF (straight rod moving in perpendicular magnetic field)
Self and mutual induction, coefficient of self-inductance and mutual inductance
Inductance of long solenoid
keyDerivations: Motional EMF expression (e = B l v)
Self-inductance of long solenoid (L = mu_0 n^2 A l)
Mutual inductance between two coaxial long solenoids
Energy stored in an inductor (U = 1/2 L I^2)
chapters.numericalFocus: Induced EMF from changing magnetic flux, self and mutual inductance calculations
diagrams: Lenz law direction schematics
Coaxial solenoids arrangement
chapters.practicalLinkage: Demonstration of Lenz's law and electromagnetic damping

coreTopics: Alternating currents, peak and RMS value of alternating current/voltage
Reactance and impedance, phase relation across resistor, inductor and capacitor
LCR series circuit (phasor diagram method), resonance, quality factor (Q factor)
Power in AC circuits, wattless current, power factor
AC generator and Transformer (step-up and step-down, energy losses)
keyDerivations: RMS vs peak value relation (I_rms = I_0 / sqrt(2))
Impedance of series LCR circuit using phasor diagram
Resonance condition and frequency (omega_r = 1 / sqrt(LC))
Average power in AC circuit (P_avg = V_rms I_rms cos phi)
Transformer turn ratio and efficiency relation
chapters.numericalFocus: LCR circuit impedance, resonant frequency, power factor, transformer secondary voltage and current
diagrams: Phasor diagrams for L, C, R and series LCR
Transformer core and coil schematics
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of AC frequency using sonometer, transformer voltage measurements

coreTopics: Basic idea of displacement current
Electromagnetic waves, their characteristics, their transverse nature (qualitative ideas only)
Electromagnetic spectrum (radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays) including elementary facts about their uses
keyDerivations: Displacement current formula (I_d = epsilon_0 dPhi_E / dt)
chapters.numericalFocus: Relation between E and B wave amplitudes (c = E_0 / B_0), frequency and wavelength calculations
diagrams: Electromagnetic wave showing mutually perpendicular E and B vectors
chapters.practicalLinkage: Detection of UV, IR radiation using sensors and prism spectrum

coreTopics: Refraction of light, total internal reflection and its applications, optical fibers
Refraction at spherical surfaces, lenses, thin lens formula, lensmaker's formula, magnification, power of a lens
Combination of thin lenses in contact
Refraction through a prism (angle of minimum deviation)
Optical instruments: Microscopes (compound) and astronomical telescopes (reflecting and refracting) and their magnifying powers
keyDerivations: Refraction at single spherical refracting surface
Lensmaker's formula (1/f = (mu - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2))
Equivalent focal length of combination of two thin lenses in contact
Prism formula (mu = sin((A+D_m)/2) / sin(A/2))
Magnifying power of Compound Microscope (normal adjustment and distinct vision)
Magnifying power of Astronomical Telescope (refracting and Cassegrain reflecting)
chapters.numericalFocus: Lensmaker formula, lens combinations, microscope and telescope tube length and magnification
diagrams: Ray diagram of compound microscope
Ray diagram of refracting and reflecting telescopes
Prism refraction diagram
chapters.practicalLinkage: To find focal length of convex lens, concave mirror; angle of minimum deviation using prism spectrometer

coreTopics: Wave front and Huygens' principle, reflection and refraction of plane wave at a plane surface using wave fronts
Proof of laws of reflection and refraction using Huygens' principle
Interference, Young's double slit experiment and expression for fringe width
Coherent sources and sustained interference of light
Diffraction due to a single slit, width of central maximum
keyDerivations: Proof of Snell's Law and Law of Reflection using Huygens wavefront construction
Expression for fringe width in Young's Double Slit Experiment (beta = lambda D / d)
Width of central diffraction maximum (2 lambda D / a)
chapters.numericalFocus: Fringe width, ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in interference, angular spread of central diffraction peak
diagrams: Huygens wavelets reflection/refraction construction
Young's double slit setup and fringe pattern
Single slit diffraction intensity curve
chapters.practicalLinkage: Laser diffraction through single and double slits in darkroom

chapters.chapterName: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
coreTopics: Dual nature of radiation, Photoelectric effect, Hertz and Lenard's observations
Einstein's photoelectric equation - particle nature of light
Experimental study of photoelectric effect (intensity, frequency, stopping potential variations)
Matter waves - wave nature of particles, de-Broglie relation
keyDerivations: Einstein's photoelectric equation (h nu = phi_0 + K_max)
de-Broglie wavelength for particle accelerated through potential V (lambda = h / sqrt(2 m q V))
chapters.numericalFocus: Threshold frequency and work function, stopping potential graphs, de Broglie wavelength of electrons and alpha particles
diagrams: Photoelectric current vs collector potential graphs
Stopping potential vs frequency graph (slope = h/e)
chapters.practicalLinkage: Photoelectric cell demonstration, solar cell IV characteristics

coreTopics: Alpha-particle scattering experiment; Rutherford's model of atom
Bohr model of hydrogen atom, postulates
Derivation of radius of nth orbit, velocity and total energy of electron in hydrogen atom
Hydrogen spectrum (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, Pfund series)
keyDerivations: Radius of nth Bohr orbit (r_n proportional to n^2)
Velocity of electron in nth orbit
Total energy of electron in nth orbit (E_n = -13.6 / n^2 eV)
Rydberg formula for spectral lines (1/lambda = R (1/n1^2 - 1/n2^2))
chapters.numericalFocus: Transition energies, maximum/minimum wavelength of spectral series, ionization potential
diagrams: Rutherford alpha scattering trajectories
Bohr energy level diagram of hydrogen with spectral transitions
chapters.practicalLinkage: Hydrogen discharge tube spectrum observation with diffraction grating

coreTopics: Composition and size of nucleus, atomic masses, isotopes, isobars, isotones
Nuclear force (properties)
Mass-energy relation, mass defect
Binding energy per nucleon and its variation with mass number
Nuclear fission and nuclear fusion
keyDerivations: Nuclear radius relation (R = R_0 A^(1/3))
Mass defect and binding energy calculation formula
chapters.numericalFocus: Binding energy per nucleon, Q-value of nuclear reactions, energy released in fission/fusion
diagrams: Binding energy per nucleon curve vs mass number A
chapters.practicalLinkage: Gieger-Muller counter radiation safety principles

chapters.chapterName: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
coreTopics: Energy bands in conductors, semiconductors and insulators (qualitative ideas only)
Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors (n-type and p-type)
p-n junction: barrier potential, depletion layer formation
Semiconductor diode: I-V characteristics in forward and reverse bias
Diode as a rectifier (Half-wave and Full-wave rectifiers with filter capacitor)
keyDerivations: Operation of half-wave and full-wave rectifier
Rectification efficiency and output ripple frequency
chapters.numericalFocus: Dynamic forward and reverse resistance from IV curve, output DC voltage and ripple frequency of rectifiers
diagrams: Energy band diagrams
Forward and reverse bias circuit diagrams and characteristic curves
Full-wave rectifier circuit with centre-tapped transformer
chapters.practicalLinkage: To draw I-V characteristics of p-n junction diode in forward and reverse bias

assessmentStructure.internalAssessment: 20 Marks (Periodic tests 10 Marks, Mathematical Activities/Portfolio/Viva 10 Marks)
assessmentStructure.questionPaperDesign: Section A (20 MCQs 1 mark each), Section B (5 VSA 2 marks), Section C (6 SA 3 marks), Section D (4 LA 5 marks), Section E (3 Case-based 4 marks each)

coreTopics: Types of relations: reflexive, symmetric, transitive and equivalence relations
One to one and onto functions (injective, surjective, bijective)
keyDerivations: Proof of equivalence relations
Verification of injectivity and surjectivity for algebraic and piecewise functions
chapters.numericalFocus: Checking equivalence classes, determining whether a function is one-one and onto for various domains
diagrams: Arrow diagrams for one-one, onto and bijective functions
chapters.practicalLinkage: Activity to verify reflexive, symmetric and transitive relations using ordered pairs

coreTopics: Definition, range, domain, principal value branch
Graphs of inverse trigonometric functions
keyDerivations: Determination of principal values
chapters.numericalFocus: Evaluating principal value expressions of sin^-1, cos^-1, tan^-1, sec^-1, cosec^-1, cot^-1
diagrams: Graphs of y = sin^-1(x), y = cos^-1(x), y = tan^-1(x)
chapters.practicalLinkage: Activity to draw graphs of inverse trigonometric functions

coreTopics: Concept, notation, order, equality, types of matrices, zero and identity matrix
Transpose of a matrix, symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices
Operation on matrices: Addition and multiplication and multiplication with a scalar
Simple properties of addition, multiplication and scalar multiplication
Non-commutativity of multiplication of matrices and existence of non-zero matrices whose product is the zero matrix
Invertible matrices and proof of the uniqueness of inverse, if it exists
keyDerivations: Uniqueness of inverse of a matrix ((AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1)
Transpose properties ((AB)' = B' A')
chapters.numericalFocus: Matrix multiplication, symmetric and skew-symmetric decomposition (A = 1/2(A+A') + 1/2(A-A')), polynomial equations in matrices
diagrams: Matrix operation tabular schemes
chapters.practicalLinkage: Construction of matrices from real-world inventory data

coreTopics: Determinant of a square matrix (up to 3 x 3 matrices)
Minors, co-factors and applications of determinants in finding the area of a triangle
Adjoint and inverse of a square matrix
Consistency, inconsistency and number of solutions of system of linear equations by examples
Solving system of linear equations in two or three variables (having unique solution) using inverse of a matrix (Matrix Method)
keyDerivations: Matrix inversion method formula (X = A^-1 B)
Adjoint properties: A(adj A) = (adj A)A = |A| I
chapters.numericalFocus: Matrix method for 3-variable simultaneous equations (guaranteed 5-mark question), area of triangle using determinants, cofactors
diagrams: 3x3 determinant cofactor sign pattern
chapters.practicalLinkage: Solving simultaneous economic/business models using matrix inversion

coreTopics: Continuity and differentiability, derivative of composite functions, chain rule, derivative of inverse trigonometric functions
Derivative of implicit functions, concept of exponential and logarithmic functions
Derivatives of logarithmic and exponential functions
Logarithmic differentiation, derivative of functions expressed in parametric forms
Second order derivatives
keyDerivations: Proof of chain rule and implicit differentiation
Second order differential equations verification
chapters.numericalFocus: Finding unknown constants k for continuity, logarithmic differentiation of variable-power-variable (e.g. x^sin x), parametric derivatives dy/dx and d^2y/dx^2
diagrams: Piecewise function continuity graphs
Vertical and horizontal tangent behaviour
chapters.practicalLinkage: Activity to explore continuity and differentiability at points of corner/cusp

coreTopics: Applications of derivatives: rate of change of quantities
Increasing/decreasing functions
Maxima and minima (first derivative test and second derivative test)
Simple problems that illustrate basic principles and understanding of the subject as well as real-life situations
keyDerivations: First and second derivative test theorems for local extrema
Optimization theorems for perimeter/volume
chapters.numericalFocus: Rate of change (ladder sliding, water draining cone), intervals of increasing/decreasing, optimization word problems (cylinders inscribed in spheres, open boxes)
diagrams: Local maxima and minima curves with tangent slopes
chapters.practicalLinkage: Activity to construct an open box of maximum volume from given cardboard sheet

coreTopics: Integration as inverse process of differentiation
Integration of a variety of functions by substitution, by partial fractions and by parts
Evaluation of standard integrals and reducible forms
Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (without proof)
Basic properties of definite integrals and evaluation of definite integrals
keyDerivations: Integration by parts formula
Definite integral king property: int_0^a f(x) dx = int_0^a f(a-x) dx
chapters.numericalFocus: Standard forms (dx/(x^2+a^2), dx/sqrt(x^2-a^2)), integration by parts with ILATE, partial fractions, definite integrals using symmetry properties
diagrams: Area under curve as limit of sums
chapters.practicalLinkage: Activity to approximate definite integral using trapezoids and rectangles

coreTopics: Applications in finding the area under simple curves, especially lines, circles/parabolas/ellipses (in standard form only)
keyDerivations: Area under standard ellipse and circle using definite integrals
chapters.numericalFocus: Area bounded between line and parabola, line and circle, standard ellipse quadrant areas
diagrams: Shaded regions between curves and coordinate axes with vertical strips
chapters.practicalLinkage: Calculating area of irregular shapes using numerical integration

coreTopics: Definition, order and degree, general and particular solutions of a differential equation
Solution of differential equations by method of separation of variables
Solutions of homogeneous differential equations of first order and first degree
Solutions of linear differential equations of the type dy/dx + P y = Q where P and Q are functions of x or constants
keyDerivations: Integrating factor IF = e^(int P dx) derivation for linear differential equations
chapters.numericalFocus: Finding order and degree, variable separable method with initial values, homogeneous substitution y = vx, integrating factor linear equations
diagrams: Family of curves representing general solution vs single particular solution
chapters.practicalLinkage: Modelling population growth and Newton's law of cooling using differential equations

coreTopics: Vectors and scalars, magnitude and direction of a vector, direction cosines and direction ratios of a vector
Types of vectors (equal, unit, zero, parallel and collinear vectors)
Position vector of a point, negative of a vector, components of a vector, addition of vectors, multiplication of a vector by a scalar
Position vector of a point dividing a line segment in a given ratio
Geometrical interpretation, properties and application of scalar (dot) product of vectors
Vector (cross) product of vectors
keyDerivations: Section formula in vector form
Dot and cross product algebraic expressions and geometric interpretations
chapters.numericalFocus: Projection of a vector on another vector, finding unit vector perpendicular to two vectors, area of triangle and parallelogram using cross product
diagrams: Right hand thumb rule for cross product
Vector addition triangle and parallelogram laws
chapters.practicalLinkage: Activity to find the angle between two vectors using scalar product

coreTopics: Direction cosines and direction ratios of a line joining two points
Cartesian equation and vector equation of a line
Skew lines and shortest distance between them (Cartesian and vector forms)
Angle between two lines
keyDerivations: Shortest distance formula between two skew lines: d = |(b1 x b2) . (a2 - a1)| / |b1 x b2|
chapters.numericalFocus: Shortest distance between skew lines (frequent 5-mark question), collinearity of three points in 3D, angle between lines from direction ratios
diagrams: 3D coordinate axes with direction angles alpha, beta, gamma
Skew lines in 3D space with shortest distance perpendicular
chapters.practicalLinkage: Physical model representation of skew lines using rods and strings

coreTopics: Introduction, related terminology such as constraints, objective function, optimization
Graphical method of solution for problems in two variables
Feasible and infeasible regions (bounded)
Feasible and infeasible solutions, optimal feasible solutions (up to three non-trivial constraints)
keyDerivations: Corner point theorem explanation
chapters.numericalFocus: Maximization and minimization of Z = ax + by with bounded feasible region, corner point evaluation method
diagrams: Cartesian inequality boundary lines and shaded feasible convex polygonal region
chapters.practicalLinkage: Solving resource optimization and diet problems using graphical linear programming

coreTopics: Conditional probability, multiplication rule on probability
Independent events, total probability
Bayes' theorem
keyDerivations: Total probability theorem proof
Bayes' theorem proof: P(E_i|A) = P(E_i)P(A|E_i) / sum(P(E_j)P(A|E_j))
chapters.numericalFocus: Bayes theorem applications (medical diagnostic tests, factory machine defective item probabilities - high weightage case study), independent events verification
diagrams: Tree diagrams for conditional and Bayes probability pathways
chapters.practicalLinkage: Simulation of medical test predictive values using Bayes theorem

assessmentStructure.practical: 30 Marks (Volumetric analysis 8, Salt analysis 8, Content based experiment 6, Project work 4, Class record and viva 4)
assessmentStructure.questionPaperDesign: Section A (16 MCQs 1 mark each), Section B (5 SA-I 2 marks), Section C (7 SA-II 3 marks), Section D (2 Case-based 4 marks each), Section E (3 LA 5 marks each)

coreTopics: Types of solutions, expression of concentration of solutions of solids in liquids
Solubility of gases in liquids (Henry's law)
Solid solutions, Raoult's law, ideal and non-ideal solutions
Colligative properties - relative lowering of vapour pressure, elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point, osmotic pressure
Determination of molecular masses using colligative properties
Abnormal molecular mass, Van't Hoff factor
keyDerivations: Raoult's law for volatile solutes
Elevation in boiling point Delta T_b = K_b * m
Depression in freezing point Delta T_f = K_f * m
Osmotic pressure pi = i C R T
Relation between van't Hoff factor i and degree of dissociation/association alpha
chapters.numericalFocus: Molarity, molality calculations, molecular mass determination from depression of freezing point, van't Hoff factor for strong/weak electrolytes
diagrams: Vapour pressure vs mole fraction graphs for ideal and non-ideal solutions (positive and negative deviations)
Freezing point depression phase curve
chapters.practicalLinkage: Preparation of standard oxalic acid / Mohr's salt solution, determination of boiling point elevation

coreTopics: Redox reactions, EMF of a cell, standard electrode potential
Nernst equation and its application to chemical cells
Relation between Gibbs energy change and EMF of a cell
Conductance in electrolytic solutions, specific and molar conductivity
Variations of conductivity and molar conductivity with concentration, Kohlrausch's Law and its applications
Electrolysis and laws of electrolysis (elementary idea)
Dry cell - electrolytic cells and Galvanic cells, lead accumulator, fuel cells, corrosion
keyDerivations: Nernst equation: E_cell = E^0_cell - (0.0591/n) log Q at 298K
Relation Delta G^0 = -n F E^0_cell and log K_c = n E^0_cell / 0.0591
Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions
chapters.numericalFocus: Cell potential using Nernst equation, equilibrium constant K_c, molar conductivity at infinite dilution, limiting molar conductivity
diagrams: Daniel cell electrochemical setup with salt bridge
Molar conductivity vs sqrt(c) for strong and weak electrolytes (Debye-Huckel-Onsager plot)
Lead storage battery reactions
chapters.practicalLinkage: Setting up Daniel cell and measuring change in potential with changing Cu2+ and Zn2+ concentrations

coreTopics: Rate of a reaction (average and instantaneous), factors affecting rates of reaction: concentration, temperature, catalyst
Order and molecularity of a reaction, rate law and specific rate constant
Integrated rate equations and half-life (only for zero and first order reactions)
Concept of collision theory (elementary ideas, no mathematical treatment)
Activation energy, Arrhenius equation
keyDerivations: Integrated rate equation for zero order reaction (k = ([R]_0 - [R])/t)
Integrated rate equation for first order reaction (k = (2.303/t) log([R]_0 / [R]))
Half-life expressions: t_1/2 = [R]_0 / (2k) for zero order, t_1/2 = 0.693 / k for first order
Arrhenius equation two-temperature form: log(k2/k1) = E_a/(2.303 R) * (1/T1 - 1/T2)
chapters.numericalFocus: Finding order from initial rate table, calculating rate constant and half-life, percentage completion time, Arrhenius activation energy calculation
diagrams: Concentration vs time graphs for zero and first order
log k vs 1/T Arrhenius plot (slope = -E_a / 2.303R)
Energy profile diagram showing activation energy with and without catalyst
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of reaction rate between sodium thiosulphate and hydrochloric acid (clock reaction)

units.unitName: d- and f-Block Elements & Coordination Compounds

coreTopics: General introduction, electronic configuration, occurrence, characteristics of transition metals

General trends in properties of first row transition metals: metallic character, ionization enthalpy, oxidation states, ionic radii, colour, catalytic property, magnetic properties, interstitial compounds, alloy formation
Preparation and properties of K2Cr2O7 and KMnO4
Lanthanoids: Electronic configuration, oxidation states, chemical reactivity and lanthanoid contraction and its consequences
Actinoids: Electronic configuration, oxidation states and comparison with lanthanoids
keyDerivations: Spin-only magnetic moment formula (mu = sqrt(n(n+2)) BM)
Balancing redox equations of KMnO4 and K2Cr2O7 in acidic medium
chapters.numericalFocus: Spin-only magnetic moment from unpaired d-electrons, oxidation state determination
diagrams: Structures of chromate, dichromate, manganate and permanganate ions
Lanthanoid contraction atomic radii trend line
chapters.practicalLinkage: Qualitative analysis of transition metal cations (Fe2+, Fe3+, Cu2+, Ni2+, Mn2+)

coreTopics: Coordination compounds: Introduction, ligands, coordination number, colour, magnetic properties and shapes
IUPAC nomenclature of mononuclear coordination compounds
Bonding, Werner's theory, VBT (Valence Bond Theory) and CFT (Crystal Field Theory)
Isomerism: Structural (linkage, coordination, ionization, hydrate) and Stereoisomerism (geometrical and optical in 4 and 6 coordinate complexes)
Importance of coordination compounds (in qualitative analysis, biological systems)
keyDerivations: Crystal field splitting in octahedral (Delta_o) and tetrahedral (Delta_t) complexes
Electronic configuration in t2g and eg sets for weak and strong field ligands
chapters.numericalFocus: Calculation of CFSE (Crystal Field Stabilization Energy), determining hybridization (sp3d2 vs d2sp3) and magnetic behaviour (inner vs outer orbital complex)
diagrams: Crystal field splitting d-orbital energy level diagram for octahedral and tetrahedral geometries
Facial and meridional geometrical isomers of Ma3b3 complexes
chapters.practicalLinkage: Preparation of potassium trioxalatoferrate(III) crystals

units.unitName: Organic Chemistry I: Haloalkanes, Alcohols and Ethers

coreTopics: Haloalkanes: Nomenclature, nature of C-X bond, physical and chemical properties, mechanism of substitution reactions (SN1 vs SN2)
Optical rotation and inversion/retention of configuration
Haloarenes: Nature of C-X bond, substitution reactions (directive influence of halogen for monosubstituted compounds only)
Uses and environmental effects of dichloromethane, trichloromethane, tetrachloromethane, iodoform, freons, DDT
keyDerivations: SN1 mechanism (two steps, carbocation intermediate, racemisation)
SN2 mechanism (single step, backside attack, transition state, Walden inversion)
Low reactivity of haloarenes towards nucleophilic substitution
chapters.numericalFocus: Order of reactivity towards SN1 and SN2, identification of chiral carbons, optical isomer count
diagrams: Walden inversion transition state diagram
Resonance structures of chlorobenzene showing partial double bond character
chapters.practicalLinkage: Silver nitrate distinction test for alkyl vs aryl halides

coreTopics: Alcohols: Nomenclature, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties (of primary alcohols only)
Identification of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols (Lucas test, copper at 573K)
Mechanism of dehydration of ethanol to ethene
Phenols: Nomenclature, methods of preparation (from cumene, diazonium salts), physical and chemical properties, acidic nature of phenol
Electrophilic aromatic substitution: Nitration, Reimer-Tiemann reaction, Kolbe's reaction
Ethers: Nomenclature, methods of preparation (Williamson synthesis), physical and chemical properties, cleavage of C-O bond by HI
keyDerivations: Acid-catalysed dehydration mechanism of ethanol to ethene
Addition of water to alkene mechanism (Markovnikov hydration)
Williamson ether synthesis mechanism and limitations
chapters.numericalFocus: Product prediction for unsymmetrical ether cleavage by HI (steric control vs carbocation stability), acidity order comparison
diagrams: Resonance structures of phenoxide ion
Mechanism schematics with curved arrows
chapters.practicalLinkage: Lucas test for 1, 2, 3 alcohols, neutral FeCl3 test for phenolic group

units.unitName: Organic Chemistry II: Aldehydes, Ketones, Carboxylic Acids, Amines & Biomolecules

coreTopics: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nomenclature, nature of carbonyl group, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties
Mechanism of nucleophilic addition, reactivity of aldehydes and ketones
Name reactions: Aldol condensation, Cross Aldol, Cannizzaro reaction, Clemmensen reduction, Wolff-Kishner reduction, Tollens test, Fehling test, Iodoform test
Carboxylic Acids: Nomenclature, acidic nature, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties
Decarboxylation and Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction
keyDerivations: Nucleophilic addition to carbonyl carbon mechanism (HCN, NaHSO3, Grignard reagent)
Aldol condensation mechanism with enolate ion
Cannizzaro hydride transfer mechanism
Acidity comparison: substituted benzoic acids vs acetic acid
chapters.numericalFocus: Organic conversion roadmaps (e.g. benzene to acetophenone, ethanol to 3-hydroxybutanal), distinction test problems
diagrams: Carbonyl dipole resonance structure
Tetrahedral intermediate in nucleophilic addition
chapters.practicalLinkage: Tollens silver mirror test, Fehling solution test, sodium bisulphite test

coreTopics: Amines: Nomenclature, classification, structure, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties
Basic character of amines (comparison in gas phase vs aqueous solution)
Identification of primary, secondary and tertiary amines (Hinsberg test, Carbylamine test, Nitrous acid test)
Diazonium salts: Preparation, chemical reactions and importance in synthetic organic chemistry (Sandmeyer, Gattermann, Azo coupling)
keyDerivations: Carbylamine test reaction
Hinsberg test mechanism with benzenesulphonyl chloride
Azo dye formation coupling reaction with phenol and beta-naphthol
chapters.numericalFocus: Order of basic strength in aqueous solution ((CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N vs (C2H5)2NH > (C2H5)3N > C2H5NH2), multi-step synthesis
diagrams: Resonance structures of benzenediazonium chloride and aniline
chapters.practicalLinkage: Carbylamine test for primary amines, azo dye test for aromatic primary amines

coreTopics: Carbohydrates: Classification (aldoses and ketoses), monosaccharides (glucose and fructose), D-L configuration
Structure of glucose (open chain and Haworth cyclic pyranose structures)
Proteins: Elementary idea of amino acids, peptide bond, polypeptides, proteins, structure of proteins (primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary)
Denaturation of proteins, enzymes
Hormones: Elementary idea excluding structure
Vitamins: Classification and deficiency diseases
Nucleic Acids: DNA and RNA, chemical composition, functions
keyDerivations: Chemical evidence for the open chain structure of glucose (HI reaction, Br2 water, HNO3, acetic anhydride)
Haworth alpha-D-glucopyranose and beta-D-glucopyranose projections
chapters.numericalFocus: Isoelectric point concepts, peptide linkage count in oligopeptides, vitamin deficiency matching
diagrams: Haworth structures of alpha and beta D-glucose and D-fructose
Double helix schematic of DNA with complementary base pairing A-T and G-C
chapters.practicalLinkage: Biuret test for proteins, Ninhydrin test for amino acids, Molisch test for carbohydrates

assessmentStructure.practical: 30 Marks (One major experiment 5, One minor experiment 4, Slide preparation 5, Spotting 7, Practical record and viva 4, Investigatory project 5)
assessmentStructure.questionPaperDesign: Section A (16 questions of 1 mark each including 4 Assertion-Reasoning), Section B (5 questions of 2 marks), Section C (7 questions of 3 marks), Section D (2 Case-based of 4 marks), Section E (3 Long questions of 5 marks)

coreTopics: Flower structure, development of male and female gametophytes
Pollination: types, agencies and examples
Outbreeding devices, pollen-pistil interaction
Double fertilization
Post-fertilization events: development of endosperm and embryo, development of seed and formation of fruit
Special modes: apomixis, parthenocarpy, polyembryony
keyDerivations: Ploidy levels of endosperm (3n), zygote (2n), aleurone layer (3n), antipodal cells (n)
chapters.numericalFocus: Calculating number of meiotic divisions required to produce N seeds, ploidy calculations
diagrams: TS of mature anther showing four microsporangia
Anatropous ovule showing embryo sac (7-celled, 8-nucleate structure)
Stages in dicot embryo development
chapters.practicalLinkage: Pollen germination on cavity slide, dissection of flower to display floral parts

coreTopics: Male and female reproductive systems
Microscopic anatomy of testis and ovary
Gametogenesis: spermatogenesis and oogenesis
Menstrual cycle
Fertilization, embryo development up to blastocyst formation, implantation
Pregnancy and placenta formation (elementary idea)
Parturition and lactation (elementary idea)
keyDerivations: Hormonal feedback loop (GnRH, LH, FSH, Estrogen, Progesterone) in menstrual cycle
chapters.numericalFocus: Oocyte counts, meiotic stages duration, sperm count viability parameters
diagrams: Diagrammatic representation of spermatogenesis and oogenesis
Hormonal levels graph during 28-day menstrual cycle (LH surge)
Sectional view of seminiferous tubule and mature Graafian follicle
chapters.practicalLinkage: Identification of TS of testis and ovary through permanent slides under compound microscope

coreTopics: Need for reproductive health and prevention of Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)
Birth control: need and methods (barrier, hormonal, IUDs, surgical)
Contraception and Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP)
Amniocentesis (significance and statutory ban)
Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART): IVF, ZIFT, GIFT, ICSI
keyDerivations: Mechanism of action of Copper-T (Cu ions suppress sperm motility) and Saheli (non-steroidal oral pill)
chapters.numericalFocus: Demographic statistics interpretation, efficacy rate comparison of contraceptives
diagrams: Vasectomy and tubectomy surgical interventions schematic
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of family planning methods and contraceptives display models

coreTopics: Mendelian inheritance, deviations from Mendelism: incomplete dominance, co-dominance, multiple alleles (ABO blood groups)
Pleiotropy, elementary idea of polygenic inheritance
Chromosome theory of inheritance
Chromosomes and genes, sex determination in humans, birds, honey bee
Linkage and crossing over (Morgan's Drosophila experiments)
Sex-linked inheritance: Haemophilia, Colour blindness
Mendelian disorders in humans: Thalassemia, Sickle cell anaemia, Phenylketonuria
Chromosomal disorders in humans: Down's syndrome, Turner's syndrome, Klinefelter's syndrome
keyDerivations: Dihybrid cross phenotypic ratio (9:3:3:1) derivation and test cross (1:1:1:1)
chapters.numericalFocus: Pedigree analysis problems, probability of offspring carrying sex-linked recessive allele, blood group inheritance crosses
diagrams: Morgan's cross showing linkage on X-chromosome of Drosophila
Pedigree charts for autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive and sex-linked traits
Karyotypes of Down's, Turner's, Klinefelter's syndromes
chapters.practicalLinkage: Pedigree charts analysis of genetic traits in human families

coreTopics: Search for genetic material: Griffith's transformation, Avery-MacLeod-McCarty, Hershey-Chase bacteriophage experiment
Structure of DNA and RNA, DNA packaging in eukaryotes (nucleosome)
DNA replication: Meselson and Stahl's semi-conservative proof, replication machinery
Transcription: transcription unit, promoter, RNA polymerase, post-transcriptional modifications (capping, tailing, splicing)
Genetic code: properties of genetic code (degenerate, unambiguous, universal, wobble)
Translation: initiation, elongation, termination, tRNA adapter molecule
Gene expression and regulation: lac Operon in E. coli
Human Genome Project (goals, salient features), DNA Fingerprinting
keyDerivations: Chargaff's rules of base equivalence (A+G = T+C)
Mechanism of lac operon in presence and absence of inducer (allolactose)
chapters.numericalFocus: Base pair count calculations, length of DNA molecule from bp count, codon and amino acid sequence decoding
diagrams: Nucleosome model showing histone octamer and H1 histone
Replication fork showing continuous and Okazaki discontinuous synthesis
lac Operon switch on/off schematic
DNA fingerprinting autoradiogram bands matching
chapters.practicalLinkage: Isolation of DNA from available plant material (spinach leaves/banana) using chilled ethanol

coreTopics: Origin of life: Oparin-Haldane chemical evolution hypothesis, Miller-Urey experiment
Biological evolution and evidences for biological evolution (palaeontology, comparative anatomy, embryology, molecular evidence)
Darwin's contribution, modern synthetic theory of evolution
Mechanism of evolution: variation (mutation and recombination) and natural selection with types (stabilizing, directional, disruptive)
Gene flow and genetic drift
Hardy-Weinberg principle and algebraic equation
Adaptive radiation (Darwin's finches, Australian marsupials)
Human evolution (Dryopithecus, Australopithecus, Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Neanderthal, Homo sapiens)
keyDerivations: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium equation derivation: p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1
chapters.numericalFocus: Calculating allele frequencies p and q, carrier frequency 2pq from disease prevalence q^2
diagrams: Miller-Urey spark discharge apparatus diagram
Homologous (divergent) vs analogous (convergent) forelimb structures
Three types of natural selection curves (stabilizing, directional, disruptive)
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of homologous and analogous organs in plants and animals from preserved specimens

coreTopics: Pathogens, parasites causing human diseases: Malaria (Plasmodium life cycle), Filariasis, Ascariasis, Typhoid, Pneumonia, Common cold, Amoebiasis, Ring worm
Basic concepts of immunology: innate and acquired immunity, active and passive immunity
Vaccines and vaccination
Structure of antibody molecule (H2L2)
Allergies, autoimmunity
Immune system in the body (primary and secondary lymphoid organs)
Cancer (causes, oncogenes, detection, treatment)
HIV and AIDS (structure, life cycle of retrovirus, transmission, prevention)
Adolescence, drug and alcohol abuse
keyDerivations: Life cycle stages of Plasmodium vivax in female Anopheles mosquito and human host
chapters.numericalFocus: Incubation periods, antibody titrations, CD4 helper T-cell counts in AIDS staging
diagrams: Plasmodium life cycle schematic in human and mosquito
Structure of an antibody molecule (variable and constant regions)
Replication of retrovirus HIV inside human macrophage and helper T-cell
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of common disease-causing organisms (Entamoeba, Plasmodium, Ascaris, Ringworm) through permanent slides

coreTopics: Microbes in household food processing (Lactobacillus, baker's yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
Microbes in industrial production (fermented beverages, antibiotics, chemicals, enzymes and other bioactive molecules e.g. cyclosporin A, statins)
Microbes in sewage treatment (primary and secondary aerobic/anaerobic biological treatment, BOD significance)
Microbes in production of biogas (methanogens Methanobacterium in anaerobic sludge digesters)
Microbes as biocontrol agents (Bacillus thuringiensis, Trichoderma, Baculoviruses/NPV)
Microbes as biofertilizers (Rhizobium, Azospirillum, Azotobacter, Mycorrhiza/Glomus, Cyanobacteria)
keyDerivations: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) inverse relation with sewage purification efficiency
chapters.numericalFocus: BOD value comparison between polluted and treated water
diagrams: Schematic diagram of sewage treatment plant (STP)
A typical biogas plant diagram with floating gas holder
chapters.practicalLinkage: Measurement of water clarity and suspended pollutants from two different water bodies

coreTopics: Genetic engineering (Recombinant DNA Technology)
Tools of recombinant DNA technology: Restriction enzymes (endonucleases, palindromic sequences, sticky ends), DNA ligase, polymerase

Cloning vectors (characteristics of ideal vector, pBR322 origin of replication, selectable markers ampR and tetR, insertional inactivation, vectors for cloning in plants Agrobacterium and animals retroviruses)
Competent host for transformation (heat shock method, microinjection, gene gun/biolistics)
Processes of recombinant DNA technology: isolation of DNA, cutting at specific sites, PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction - denaturation, annealing, extension)
Bioreactors (stirred tank, sparged) and downstream processing
keyDerivations: PCR amplification formula: 2^n copies after n cycles
Insertional inactivation mechanism of beta-galactosidase gene (blue-white screening)
chapters.numericalFocus: Amplification yield after n cycles of PCR, restriction digest fragment sizing
diagrams: E. coli cloning vector pBR322 restriction map
Steps in recombinant DNA technology using foreign DNA and vector DNA
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) steps
Simple stirred-tank and sparged stirred-tank bioreactors
chapters.practicalLinkage: Agarose gel electrophoresis demonstration and DNA band visualization under UV illuminator

coreTopics: Applications of biotechnology in agriculture: genetically modified organisms (Bt cotton - Cry proteins and insect resistance, RNA interference/RNAi in Meloidogyne incognita resistance)

Applications in medicine: genetically engineered insulin (Humulin proinsulin processing), gene therapy (ADA deficiency treatment using retroviral vector into lymphocytes), molecular diagnosis (ELISA, PCR)
Transgenic animals: reasons for creating transgenic models (physiology, disease study, biological products alpha-1-antitrypsin, vaccine safety testing, chemical safety testing)
Biosafety and ethical issues, biopiracy and patenting of indigenous resources
keyDerivations: RNA interference (RNAi) mechanism: dsRNA cleavage by Dicer into siRNA and RISC silencing of viral/nematode mRNA
chapters.numericalFocus: Analysis of transgenic livestock yield efficiency, ELISA optical density correlations
diagrams: Maturation of pro-insulin into active insulin by removal of C-peptide
RNA interference cellular defense mechanism pathway
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of GM crops samples (Bt cotton boll vs non-Bt boll damage comparison)

coreTopics: Population: population attributes (birth rate, death rate, sex ratio, age pyramids - expanding, stable, declining)
Population growth: factors affecting population size (natality, mortality, immigration, emigration)
Growth models: exponential growth (J-shaped, dN/dt = rN) and logistic growth (S-shaped Verhulst-Pearl logistic, dN/dt = rN((K-N)/K))
Population interactions: Mutualism, Competition (Gause's competitive exclusion principle), Predation, Parasitism, Commensalism, Amensalism
keyDerivations: Exponential growth equation: N_t = N_0 e^(rt)
Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth equation derivation with carrying capacity K
chapters.numericalFocus: Calculating intrinsic rate of natural increase r, population size projection after t generations, carrying capacity evaluations
diagrams: Age pyramids for human population (expanding, stable, declining)
Exponential and logistic population growth curves
Mutualistic interactions (fig and wasp, lichen, mycorrhiza)
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of plant population density and frequency by quadrat method

coreTopics: Ecosystems: patterns, components, productivity and decomposition
Energy flow: food chains, food webs, 10% law of energy transfer (Lindeman)
Pyramids of number, biomass and energy (upright vs inverted pyramids)
Ecological succession (primary and secondary, hydrarch and xerarch succession)
Nutrient cycling and ecosystem services (carbon/phosphorus cycles, Robert Costanza valuation)
keyDerivations: 10 percent law energy transfer calculations along trophic levels
chapters.numericalFocus: Trophic level energy transfer efficiency, primary vs secondary productivity (GPP - R = NPP)
diagrams: Pyramid of biomass in sea (inverted) vs terrestrial (upright)
Ecological succession stages from pioneer to climax community
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of aquatic ecosystem food chain and trophic levels

coreTopics: Concept of biodiversity, levels of biodiversity (genetic, species, ecological)
Patterns of biodiversity: latitudinal gradients, species-area relationships (Alexander von Humboldt)
Importance of biodiversity: David Tilman's plots, Paul Ehrlich's 'Rivet popper hypothesis'
Loss of biodiversity: causes - 'The Evil Quartet' (habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions, co-extinctions)

Biodiversity conservation: in-situ conservation (National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, sacred groves) and ex-situ conservation (zoological parks, botanical gardens, cryopreservation, seed banks)
International conventions: Earth Summit (Rio de Janeiro 1992), World Summit (Johannesburg 2002)
keyDerivations: Species-area relationship equation: log S = log C + Z log A (regression coefficient Z)
chapters.numericalFocus: Calculating species richness using logarithmic species-area relation, percentage of threatened species across taxa
diagrams: Species-area relationship rectangular hyperbola and log-log straight line graph
Global pie charts showing representation of taxa (invertebrates, vertebrates, plants)
chapters.practicalLinkage: Documentation of biodiversity in local school campus or botanical garden

units.unitName: The Rajasthani and Pahari Schools of Miniature Painting

chapters.chapterName: The Rajasthani School of Miniature Painting
coreTopics: Origin and development of Rajasthani School (16th to 19th century A.D.)
Sub-schools of Rajasthani style: Mewar, Bundi, Jodhpur, Bikaner, Kishangarh, Jaipur
Main features and characteristics of Rajasthani School (human forms, glowing colors, themes of Radha-Krishna, nature and seasons)
Study of Prescribed Paintings: Maru Ragini (Mewar), Chaugan Players (Jodhpur), Krishna on Swing (Bikaner), Radha (Bani-Thani) by Nihal Chand (Kishangarh), Bharat Meets Rama at Chitrakuta (Jaipur)
keyDerivations: Artistic style analysis and symbolic representation in Bani-Thani by Nihal Chand
chapters.numericalFocus: Chronological timeline of sub-schools and royal patrons
diagrams: Color palette and compositional geometry in Mewar and Kishangarh paintings
chapters.practicalLinkage: Study of miniature painting brush techniques, natural pigments preparation

chapters.chapterName: The Pahari School of Miniature Painting
coreTopics: Origin and development of Pahari School in Himalayan sub-states (17th to 19th century A.D.)
Sub-schools: Basohli, Guler, Kangra, Chamba, Garhwal
Main features: lyrical charm, rhythmic lines, tranquil female depictions, Bhagavata Purana and Gita Govinda themes
Study of Prescribed Paintings: Krishna with Gopis (Basohli School by Manaku), Nand, Yashoda and Krishna with Kinsmen going to Vrindavana (Kangra School by Nainsukh)
keyDerivations: Comparison of bold Basohli style vs delicate lyrical Kangra line work
chapters.numericalFocus: Historical dating of Nainsukh and Manaku royal ateliers
diagrams: Compositional analysis of Krishna with Gopis and landscape backdrop
chapters.practicalLinkage: Landscape composition in watercolor using wash and tempera methods

units.unitName: The Mughal and Deccan Schools of Miniature Painting

chapters.chapterName: The Mughal School of Miniature Painting
coreTopics: Origin and development under Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, and decline under Aurangzeb
Synthesis of Persian, indigenous Indian and European realistic elements
Features: calligraphic borders (hashiya), portraiture (shabih), durbar scenes, flora and fauna

Study of Prescribed Paintings: Krishna Lifting Mount Govardhan (Miskin, Akbar atelier), Falcon on a Bird-Rest (Ustad Mansur, Jahangir atelier), Kabir and Raidas (Ustad Faquirullah Khan, Shah Jahan atelier), Marriage Procession of Dara Shikoh (Haji Madani)
keyDerivations: Naturalistic bird depiction and master shading in Ustad Mansur's Falcon on a Bird-Rest
chapters.numericalFocus: Reign periods of Mughal emperors and development phases of the imperial atelier
diagrams: Ornate border decoration (hashiya) motifs and perspective layering
chapters.practicalLinkage: Object study with precise gouache brushwork and delicate shading

chapters.chapterName: The Deccan School of Miniature Painting
coreTopics: Origin and development in southern sultanates: Ahmednagar, Bijapur, Golconda, Hyderabad
Features: rich sensuous colors, Persian delicacy merged with South Indian warmth, use of gold and tall slender figures
Study of Prescribed Paintings: Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya and Amir Khusro (Hyderabad School), Chand Bibi Playing Polo (Golconda/Bijapur)
keyDerivations: Symbolic interaction between saint and poet in Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya and Amir Khusro
chapters.numericalFocus: Sultanate patronage timelines and European trade influence
diagrams: Color harmony and architectural backdrops in Deccani miniatures
chapters.practicalLinkage: Color mixing and tempera layering exercise

units.unitName: The Bengal School of Painting and the Modern Trends in Indian Art

coreTopics: Nationalist revival of Indian art: E.B. Havell, Abanindranath Tagore, Sister Nivedita
Swadeshi movement in art, departure from Western academic realism towards Ajanta, Mughal and Japanese wash technique
Study of Prescribed Paintings: Journey's End (Abanindranath Tagore), Shiva and Sati (Nandalal Bose), Radhika (M.A.R. Chughtai), Meghdoot (Ram Gopal Vijaivargiya)
keyDerivations: Emotional pathos and symbolism in Abanindranath Tagore's Journey's End (collapsing camel)
chapters.numericalFocus: Indian Society of Oriental Art milestones and Kala Bhavana Santiniketan establishment
diagrams: Japanese wash technique layering process diagram
chapters.practicalLinkage: Watercolor wash painting demonstration on handmade paper

chapters.chapterName: Modern Trends in Indian Art (Paintings, Graphic Prints and Sculptures)
coreTopics: Introduction to contemporary and modern movements: Progressive Artists' Group (PAG), Cholamandal Artists' Village
Prescribed Modern Paintings: Rama Vanquishing the Pride of the Ocean (Raja Ravi Varma), Mother and Child (Jamini Roy), Haldi Grinders (Amrita Sher-Gil), Mother Teresa (M.F. Husain)
Prescribed Graphic Prints: Whirlpool (Krishna Reddy), Children (Somnath Hore), Devi (Jyoti Bhatt), Of Walls (Anupam Sud)

Prescribed Modern Sculptures: Triumph of Labour (D.P. Roy Chowdhury, bronze), Santhal Family (Ramkinkar Baij, cement and pebble), Cries Un-heard (Amar Nath Sehgal, bronze), Ganesha (P.V. Jankiram, oxidized copper)
keyDerivations: Folk art revivalist elements in Jamini Roy's flat colors and bold sweeping brush lines

diagrams: Sculptural balance and dynamic tension in Triumph of Labour
